evaluation_protocol.name: Active Service Evaluation Protocol
evaluation_protocol.description: Evaluates the ability of a memory system to generate unsolicited alerts based on logical constraints over stored personal state. Each scenario distributes facts across multiple sessions and requires computation, constraint checking, or cross-referencing that pure similarity-based retrieval cannot perform.

scoring.alert_generated: Did the system generate an unsolicited alert? (binary)
scoring.severity_correct: Was the severity level appropriate? (critical / warning / info)
scoring.timing_correct: Was the alert triggered at the right session? (binary)
scoring.reasoning_correct: Did the alert include correct computation or logic? (binary)
scoring.message_actionable: Was the alert message actionable and specific? (1-5 scale)

scenarios.description: Passport expires within the 6-month validity window required by Japan

sessions.conversation:
User: Hey, just picked up my renewed passport today. New expiry is March 5, 2025. What a relief to finally get that sorted.
Assistant: Great that you got it taken care of! I've noted your new passport expiration date of March 5, 2025. Let me know if there's anything else I can help with.

User: So exciting — I just booked flights to Tokyo! Departing February 20th, coming back March 1st. Can you help me think about what to pack?
Assistant: That sounds wonderful! I'd love to help with packing. Before we get to that though, I need to flag something important...

trigger_session.description: Trip booking triggers constraint check against stored passport expiration date and Japan's entry requirements

expected_alert.message: Your passport expires March 5, 2025 -- only 13 days after your February 20 departure to Japan. Japan requires at least 6 months (180 days) of passport validity from date of entry. You need a passport valid until at least August 19, 2025.
expected_alert.computation: (2025-03-05) - (2025-02-20) = 13 days remaining validity; required = 180 days; 13 < 180 = VIOLATION

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires date arithmetic (computing days between expiry and departure), knowledge of Japan's 6-month validity rule, and comparing the result. No embedding similarity search can perform calendar math.

scenarios.description: Transit through China requires a transit visa the user does not have

sessions.conversation:
User: I hold a Canadian passport, if that matters for anything travel-related.
Assistant: Good to know! I've noted that you hold a Canadian passport. That'll be helpful for any future travel planning.

Assistant: That's a long layover! Before you decide, I should mention something important...

trigger_session.description: Flight booking with Beijing layover triggers transit visa requirement check for Canadian passport holders

expected_alert.message: A 14-hour layover in Beijing requires a Chinese transit visa for Canadian passport holders unless you qualify for the 24/72/144-hour visa-free transit policy. You would need to confirm eligibility for the visa-free transit, which requires staying in designated transit areas or cities. Without proper documentation, you could be denied boarding.
expected_alert.computation: Canadian passport + 14-hour Beijing layover = transit visa or visa-free transit eligibility required

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires cross-referencing nationality (stored in session 2) with transit country requirements (world knowledge) and layover duration. Similarity search for 'Bangkok flights' would not surface passport nationality or visa rules.

expected_alert.computation: single-entry visa + 1 prior entry (Paris, November) = 0 entries remaining; Berlin trip requires 1 entry = VIOLATION

Assistant: How exciting for Lily! I've noted that her passport is under the name Lily Chen.

User: Just booked the whole family for a trip to Mexico -- me, Tom, and little Lily Anderson. Departing March 10.
Assistant: A family trip to Mexico sounds lovely! I want to flag something about Lily's booking...

trigger_session.description: Flight booked under 'Lily Anderson' but passport reads 'Lily Chen'

expected_alert.message: Lily's passport is under the name 'Lily Chen' (from session on August 10), but the flight was booked under 'Lily Anderson.' Airlines require the ticket name to match the passport exactly. You'll need to either update the flight booking to 'Lily Chen' or get Lily's passport reissued under 'Lily Anderson.'
expected_alert.computation: passport_name('Lily Chen') != booking_name('Lily Anderson') = NAME MISMATCH

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires connecting a name change event (wedding) to the implication that the child's documents are now mismatched. The booking under 'Anderson' seems normal post-wedding, but the passport was never updated.

expected_alert.computation: blank_pages(1) < required_pages(2 for India: 1 visa + 1 stamps) = VIOLATION

scenarios.description: Schengen 90/180 day rule will be exceeded by planned trip

User: Just got back from 45 days in Europe -- spent time in France, Italy, and Spain. Left on April 15 and came back today.
Assistant: Sounds like an incredible European adventure! 45 days across three countries.

trigger_session.description: Third Schengen trip would exceed 90-day limit within 180-day rolling window

expected_alert.message: You've already spent approximately 75 days in the Schengen area in the last 180 days (45 days from April 15 - June 1, and 30 days from July 1 - July 20). A 21-day trip starting September 5 would bring your total to 96 days, exceeding the 90-day limit within any 180-day period. You can only stay up to 15 more days before October 12, 2024.
expected_alert.computation: days_used = 45 + 30 = 75; planned = 21; total = 96; limit = 90; 96 > 90 = VIOLATION; remaining = 90 - 75 = 15 days

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires aggregating stay durations across multiple sessions, computing a rolling 180-day window, and performing arithmetic to determine remaining allowance. This is multi-session state accumulation plus date math.

scenarios.description: Newly prescribed SSRI conflicts with existing MAOI

sessions.conversation:
User: My psychiatrist put me on phenelzine for my depression. It's an older medication but she thinks it might work better for me.
Assistant: I hope it helps! Phenelzine is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor -- it can be quite effective. I've noted this as a current medication.

User: Saw a different doctor while traveling and she prescribed sertraline (Zoloft) for anxiety. Should I start taking it?
Assistant: I need to urgently flag a serious safety concern before you take sertraline...

trigger_session.description: New SSRI prescription triggers interaction check against existing MAOI

expected_alert.message: DANGEROUS INTERACTION: Sertraline (SSRI) combined with phenelzine (MAOI) can cause serotonin syndrome, a potentially fatal condition. These two medications should never be taken together. There should be at least a 14-day washout period after stopping phenelzine before starting sertraline. Contact your psychiatrist immediately before taking the sertraline.
expected_alert.computation: phenelzine(MAOI) + sertraline(SSRI) = serotonin_syndrome_risk = CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATION

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires pharmacological knowledge to identify drug classes (MAOI + SSRI) and their interaction risk. Embedding similarity between 'phenelzine' and 'sertraline' is low -- they are different drug names mentioned months apart.

scenarios.description: Prescribed antibiotic conflicts with known penicillin allergy

sessions.conversation:
User: Quick question -- do you know any good non-penicillin antibiotics? I'm allergic to penicillin. Found out the hard way as a kid, got hives everywhere.
Assistant: Sorry to hear about the allergy! Yes, there are many alternatives. I've noted your penicillin allergy. Some common alternatives include azithromycin, fluoroquinolones, and others depending on the infection.

User: Got a sinus infection. The urgent care doc prescribed amoxicillin. Picking it up from the pharmacy later today.
Assistant: Wait -- I need to alert you about something critical before you fill that prescription...

trigger_session.description: Amoxicillin prescription triggers allergy check; amoxicillin is a penicillin-type antibiotic

expected_alert.message: Amoxicillin is a penicillin-type antibiotic, and you have a documented penicillin allergy (hives). There is significant cross-reactivity between amoxicillin and penicillin. Do NOT take amoxicillin. Contact the prescribing doctor and mention your penicillin allergy to get an alternative antibiotic.
expected_alert.computation: amoxicillin ∈ penicillin_class; user_allergy = penicillin; cross_reactivity = HIGH = CONTRAINDICATED

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires knowing that amoxicillin belongs to the penicillin drug class. The user said 'penicillin allergy' and was prescribed 'amoxicillin' -- these are different words with no surface-level similarity, but pharmacologically they are in the same class.

scenarios.description: Grapefruit consumption interacts with statin medication

sessions.conversation:
User: Doctor put me on simvastatin for cholesterol. 40mg daily. Hoping to get my numbers down without changing my diet too much.
Assistant: Simvastatin is a common choice for cholesterol management. I've noted your prescription -- 40mg daily. Regular follow-ups to check your levels would be a good idea.

User: I'm starting a new health kick! Going to drink fresh grapefruit juice every morning. Already bought a juicer and a case of grapefruits.
Assistant: I love the healthy initiative! But I need to flag an important interaction...

trigger_session.description: Grapefruit consumption plan triggers food-drug interaction check against simvastatin

expected_alert.message: Grapefruit juice significantly increases simvastatin levels in your blood by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme that metabolizes the drug. This can increase the risk of serious side effects including muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis). You should avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking simvastatin, or ask your doctor about switching to a statin that isn't affected (like rosuvastatin or pravastatin).
expected_alert.computation: simvastatin(CYP3A4 substrate) + grapefruit(CYP3A4 inhibitor) = elevated_drug_levels = RISK

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires connecting a dietary change to a stored medication via enzyme metabolism pathways. 'Grapefruit juice' and 'simvastatin' have zero semantic similarity, but their interaction is clinically significant.

expected_alert.computation: allergy(shellfish, severity=anaphylaxis) + restaurant(shellfish-focused) = HIGH cross_contamination_risk

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires connecting 'The Crab Shack' (a restaurant name) to shellfish via common sense, then cross-referencing against a stored allergy from months prior. No direct textual overlap between the allergy discussion and the restaurant booking.

scenarios.description: Dosage exceeds safe limit given user's recorded body weight

sessions.conversation:
User: Just had my annual physical. I weigh 52 kg -- doctor says I'm on the lighter side but healthy.
Assistant: Glad to hear you're healthy! 52 kg is noted.

User: I have a terrible toothache. The dentist prescribed ibuprofen 800mg three times a day. That seems like a lot to me -- is it?
Assistant: I want to check on that dosage given your body weight...

trigger_session.description: Ibuprofen dosage triggers weight-based safety check

expected_alert.message: At 52 kg body weight, your prescribed ibuprofen dose of 2400 mg/day (800mg x 3) is at the absolute maximum adult daily limit regardless of weight. For your weight, a more typical therapeutic dose would be around 1200-1600 mg/day. While 2400 mg/day is technically within FDA limits for short-term use, you should confirm with your dentist that this high dose is intentional for your body weight, and ensure you take it with food to protect your stomach.
expected_alert.computation: dose_daily = 800mg * 3 = 2400mg; max_adult_daily = 3200mg; weight_adjusted_typical = ~10mg/kg * 3 doses = 1560mg; 2400 > 1560 = elevated for weight

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires recalling body weight from a different medical context (annual physical) and applying weight-based dosing guidelines to a dental prescription. The two sessions are thematically unrelated.

scenarios.description: Planned scuba diving is contraindicated with asthma medication

sessions.conversation:
User: My asthma has been acting up lately. Doctor increased my Advair dose and added montelukast. Using my rescue inhaler about twice a week.
Assistant: Sorry to hear the asthma is flaring up. I've noted the Advair increase and montelukast addition. Twice-weekly rescue inhaler use suggests it's not fully controlled -- hopefully the new regimen helps.

User: I signed up for a PADI scuba diving certification course in Cozumel next month! Always been on my bucket list.
Assistant: Scuba diving is an amazing experience! But I need to raise a health concern...

trigger_session.description: Scuba diving plan triggers asthma contraindication check

expected_alert.message: Scuba diving with poorly controlled asthma is considered a significant risk. As of your last update, you were using your rescue inhaler twice weekly, which indicates your asthma is not fully controlled. Diving with asthma increases the risk of air trapping, pulmonary barotrauma, and arterial gas embolism. Most dive medical authorities require asthma to be well-controlled (no rescue inhaler use for 48+ hours, normal spirometry) before clearing someone to dive. You should get a dive medical clearance from a physician familiar with dive medicine before the course.
expected_alert.computation: asthma(poorly_controlled, rescue_inhaler_2x/week) + scuba_diving = ELEVATED risk of barotrauma

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires connecting recreational activity planning to a medical condition discussed in a completely different context. 'Scuba diving' and 'asthma inhaler' have no semantic overlap for retrieval.

scenarios.description: Warfarin patient starts taking high-dose vitamin K supplements

sessions.conversation:
User: Been on warfarin for about two years now after the blood clot. INR has been stable at 2.5 -- doc is happy with it.
Assistant: Good to hear your INR is stable. Consistent warfarin management is important. I've noted your warfarin use and stable INR.

User: My friend told me about this amazing supplement stack for bone health. I just ordered vitamin K2 (200mcg), calcium, and vitamin D3. Should arrive tomorrow.
Assistant: Bone health is important! However, I need to warn you about one of those supplements...

trigger_session.description: Vitamin K supplement directly antagonizes warfarin therapy

expected_alert.message: Vitamin K directly counteracts warfarin. Warfarin works by inhibiting vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, so supplementing with vitamin K2 (200mcg) could significantly reduce warfarin's effectiveness, destabilize your INR, and increase your risk of blood clots. Do NOT start the vitamin K2 supplement without consulting the doctor managing your warfarin therapy. The calcium and vitamin D3 are generally fine.
expected_alert.computation: warfarin(vitamin_K_antagonist) + vitamin_K2_supplement(200mcg) = therapeutic_antagonism = CONTRAINDICATED

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires understanding that vitamin K is the specific mechanism warfarin inhibits -- a pharmacological relationship, not a textual one. 'Bone health supplements' and 'blood clot medication' are completely different topics in embedding space.

This requires immediate medical attention.
expected_alert.computation: isotretinoin(category_X_teratogen) + pregnancy = SEVERE birth_defect_risk; prescription_start(June) + 5_month_course = still_active(September) = IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED

scenarios.why_retrieval_fails: Requires connecting a dermatology prescription to pregnancy safety categories, and computing whether the medication course is still active. 'Pregnancy' and 'acne medication' are semantically distant topics.
